📢 [ENGLISH VERSION] - Microphone Input System Documentation

Overview
Microphone Input System allows you to control character animations dynamically based on an audio clip (e.g., imported MP3 voicelines), including volume detection. It supports dialogue playlists (arrays of voicelines + subtitles + per-line mouth toggle).

Supported Animations:
- Head Rotation (Angle Mode)
- Skinned Mesh BlendShape control (BlendShape Mode)
- Text Output (Intensity Mode)
- Position Shifting (Position Mode)
- Sprite Swapping (SpriteSwap Mode)

How to Setup
1. Add the MicrophoneInputSystem script to a GameObject.
2. On MicrophoneManager (Inspector), fill:
    - voiceLines (AudioClip array)
    - mouthShouldMove (bool array aligned to voiceLines)
    - subtitles (string array aligned to voiceLines)
    - transitionDelays (float array, seconds to wait before moving to the next line)
    - subtitleTextTarget (assign your TMP text object for captions)
    - audiblePlayback (toggle whether you hear the audio)
   (If you leave arrays empty, it will fall back to the single voiceClip field.)
3. Optionally assign a TMP text field to MicrophoneInputSystem.subtitleTextTarget (overrides manager target).
4. Choose the Voice Target Mode in the Inspector.
5. Assign the relevant target object depending on the mode:
    - Angle/Position Mode → Assign a Transform
    - BlendShape Mode → Assign a SkinnedMeshRenderer and (optionally) a BlendShape name
    - Intensity Mode → Assign a TextMeshPro object
    - SpriteSwap Mode → Assign a SpriteRenderer and mouth Sprites

Options Explanation
- Sensitivity: Controls the response power based on clip loudness.
- Smooth Speed: Controls the animation transition smoothness.

Important Notes
- Import your MP3/WAV/OGG files as AudioClips and assign them to MicrophoneManager.voiceLines (or leave arrays empty to use MicrophoneManager’s single clip).
- MicrophoneManager is required for playlist data.
- Inspector warnings will notify you if critical fields are missing.
- No microphone permissions are required; audio can play audibly (toggle in Inspector) while still driving animations.
- Designed to be lightweight and compatible with mobile and desktop platforms.
